senses.definition: The action of defending, of protecting from attack, danger or injury.

quotes.text:
In cases of defence ’tis best to weigh
The enemy more mighty than he seems:
quotes.reference: 1599 (date written), William Shakespeare, “The Life of Henry the Fift”, in Mr. William Shakespeares Comedies, Histories, & Tragedies […] (First Folio), London: […] Isaac Iaggard, and Ed[ward] Blount, published 1623, →OCLC, [Act II, scene iv]:

quotes.text:
And nothing ’gainst Time’s scythe can make defence
Save breed, to brave him when he takes thee hence.

quotes.text:

Against thy reasons making no defence.

quotes.text: But the Danes remained resolute in defence - largely thanks to a spirited display by captain Daniel Agger - and they went ahead with their first meaningful attack.

senses.definition: (team sports) The portion of a team dedicated to preventing the other team from scoring; contrasted with offence.

quotes.text: The most persistent tormentor was Alex Oxlade-Chamberlain, who scored a hat-trick in last month’s corresponding fixture in Iceland. His ability to run at defences is instantly striking, but it is his clever use of possession that has persuaded some shrewd judges that he is an even better prospect than Theo Walcott.

quotes.text: Better manned and more strongly defenced.
